rubrics: The response should state the drone’s most likely immediate flight-mode/behavior outcomes in order when LED headlights shine directly at the drone with marginal VIO and GPS signals and a hand landing is attempted. For example, it will transition to Attitude Mode, then obstacle avoidance will be disabled, then it will adopt emergency landing behavior.
The response should include a safety-first recommendation  for the user. For example, “Avoid hand landing as it is not recommended and can cause bodily harm”

The response should suggest safer alternatives for the user when the scenario can result in bodily harm. For example, "Instead of attempting a dangerous hand landing, command an autonomous Return/Land or move to a safe landing site.”

The response should reference specific pages and sections with precise guidance from the provided Skydio X10 Operator Manual excerpt that justify any major claim. For example, "For the “do not hand land at night” warning (see, 'Flying at night' section, page 6)."

The response should mention that the lights turn yellow to visually indicate that the drone is below 10 ft (3 m), which indicates that obstacle avoidance is disabled during landing and hand-catching is risky.

The response should explain how direct and bright artificial light (for example, car LED headlights) can affect the visual navigation system of the drone and could trigger a “sudden transition into Attitude Mode” according to the manual.
The response should have a clear and distinct section addressing how the drone will respond. For example, "How the Drone Will Respond".
The response should have a clear and distinct section addressing why the drone will respond in the way that it does. For example, "Why the Drone Will Respond This Way".
The response should have a clear and distinct section addressing the safety risks that are present when flying in the scenario described in the user prompt. For example, "Safety Risks Present".
The response should detail the three operational risks of Attitude mode:  continuous manual control needed, no obstacle avoidance, and drift when sticks are centered.
